paragraphs.title: The Invitation and the Hesitation to Open

answers: His garden
The city
The house of the watchmen
easy.explanation: He says, “I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse.”
easy.q: What does the beloved say he has entered?

answers: The voice of the watchmen
The voice of her beloved knocking
The daughters of Jerusalem calling
easy.explanation: She hears “the voice of my beloved that knocketh.”

answers: She is angry
She is fully awake
She sleeps, but her heart is awake
easy.explanation: She says, “I sleep, but my heart waketh.”
easy.q: What condition does the woman describe?

answers: She has taken off her coat and washed her feet
She does not know who is outside
She is speaking with the daughters of Jerusalem
medium.explanation: She has already settled down to rest, saying, “I have put off my coat” and washed her feet.
medium.q: Why does the woman hesitate to open the door?

answers: The woman opens the door, the beloved enters, and the watchmen leave
The beloved invites her, she hears him knocking, and she hesitates to open
The watchmen arrive, the beloved calls, and the woman goes to sleep

medium.q: Which sequence best describes the passage?

answers: Sings loudly
Calls from far away
Strikes or taps on the door
medium.explanation: “Knocketh” means that the beloved is tapping or striking at the door.
medium.q: What does “knocketh” mean in this passage?

answers: She is completely unaware of the beloved
Her body rests while she remains inwardly aware of him
She does not know who is outside
challenge.explanation: The contrast shows that although she is physically resting, her heart remains alert to the beloved.
challenge.q: What contrast is expressed by “I sleep, but my heart waketh”?

answers: It presents love as a joyful invitation to share together
It emphasizes the woman’s loneliness
It explains why the watchmen pursue her
challenge.explanation: The beloved invites friends and beloved ones to participate in celebration and love.
challenge.q: How does the invitation to eat and drink fit the passage?

answers: The watchmen going about the city
The beloved’s head being filled with dew
The woman’s coat and washed feet
challenge.explanation: Taking off a coat and washing the feet suggest preparation for sleep and rest.
challenge.q: Which detail most strongly creates an atmosphere of night and rest?

paragraphs.title: The Missed Meeting and the Search

answers: The beloved putting his hand through the door
The words of the daughters of Jerusalem
The appearance of the watchmen
easy.explanation: When the beloved puts his hand through the door, her heart is moved for him.

answers: She goes back to sleep
She rises to seek him
She asks the watchmen to bring him to her
easy.explanation: She says, “I sought him, but I could not find him.”
easy.q: What does the woman do after the beloved is gone?

answers: The beloved
The watchmen
The daughters of Jerusalem
easy.explanation: She charges the daughters of Jerusalem to tell her beloved that she is lovesick.
easy.q: To whom does the woman speak at the end of the passage?

answers: His reaching hand awakens her love
The watchmen command her to rise
The daughters of Jerusalem call her
medium.explanation: Her heart is moved by him, so she rises to open the door.
medium.q: Why does the woman rise to open to the beloved?

answers: The beloved remains with her
The beloved withdraws himself and is gone
The watchmen bring him into the city
medium.explanation: The text says, “my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone.”
medium.q: What happens after the woman opens the door?

answers: A covering or outer garment
A key
A vessel for perfume
medium.explanation: The watchmen take away her veil, which is a covering or outer garment.
medium.q: In this context, what is a “veil”?

answers: Only anger toward the beloved
Indifference to his disappearance
The great intensity of her longing and love
challenge.explanation: “Sick of love” describes the overwhelming strength of her desire for the absent beloved.
challenge.q: What does the woman’s statement that she is “sick of love” express?

answers: The beloved disappears, the woman rises, and then he reaches through the door
The beloved reaches through the door, the woman rises, he disappears, and she searches for him
The watchmen find the beloved, the woman meets him, and she returns home
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the beloved’s reaching hand, her rising, his disappearance, and her search.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events appears in the passage?

answers: They help her find the beloved
They stop her and mistreat her
They deliver a message from the beloved
challenge.explanation: The watchmen smite and wound her and take away her veil, preventing them from helping her.
challenge.q: How do the watchmen affect the woman’s search?

paragraphs.title: The Question About the Beloved’s Identity

answers: The daughters of Jerusalem
The watchmen
The friends
easy.explanation: The daughters of Jerusalem ask, “What is thy beloved more than another beloved?”
easy.q: Who asks the woman questions about her beloved?

answers: Where the garden is
What makes the beloved special
Who the watchmen are
easy.explanation: They ask what distinguishes her beloved from another beloved.
easy.q: What do the daughters of Jerusalem want to know?

answers: He is standing beside them
The woman has forgotten him
His identity or whereabouts are not clear to them
easy.explanation: Their question shows that they do not yet understand what makes him so special or where he is.
easy.q: What does their question suggest about the beloved?

answers: They want to understand why the woman seeks him so intensely
They have already found him
They want the woman to return to sleep
medium.explanation: Their question seeks an explanation for the woman’s passionate search and longing.
medium.q: Why do the daughters of Jerusalem ask what is special about the beloved?

answers: It shows that they know exactly where he is
It shows that they do not know his location or distinction
It shows that they saw him enter the garden
medium.explanation: They ask about him because neither his whereabouts nor his unique qualities are known to them.
medium.q: How is their question connected with the beloved’s disappearance?

answers: What makes your beloved different or better than another
When will your beloved arrive
Where did your beloved come from
medium.explanation: The phrase asks what distinguishes the woman’s beloved from other beloved ones.
medium.q: What does the phrase “more than another beloved” ask?

answers: The focus moves from searching for the beloved to explaining his uniqueness
The focus moves from praising him to becoming angry with him
The focus moves from resting to preparing for sleep
challenge.explanation: The woman expresses her longing, and the daughters then ask what makes the beloved worthy of such devotion.
challenge.q: What conceptual movement occurs between the woman’s words and the daughters’ question?

answers: They have found him but are hiding him
They do not know where he is
They do not want to help the woman
challenge.explanation: Their question indicates that the beloved is not present and his location is unknown.
challenge.q: What can be inferred because the daughters ask about the beloved instead of saying where he is?

answers: It leads to a detailed description of the beloved’s beauty
It leads to a description of the city watchmen
It leads to the woman returning to rest
challenge.explanation: The woman answers by describing the beloved’s appearance in detail.
challenge.q: How does this question prepare for the rest of the chapter?

answers: Gold, precious stones, spices, flowers, and cedars
Houses, gates, and ships
Tools, garments, and towers
easy.explanation: The description uses images of gold, jewels, spices, flowers, marble, Lebanon, and cedars.
easy.q: What images does the woman use to describe the beloved?

answers: Dark and pale
White and ruddy
Green and golden
easy.explanation: The woman says, “My beloved is white and ruddy.”
easy.q: How is the beloved’s complexion described?

answers: By saying that he is gone
By saying that he guards the city
By calling him both beloved and friend
easy.explanation: The passage ends, “This is my beloved, and this is my friend.”

answers: They provide only practical identification details
They express the beloved as an ideal of beauty in the woman’s eyes
They describe the streets where he walks
medium.explanation: The rich imagery presents him as extraordinarily beautiful and precious to her.
medium.q: What is the effect of the many images used in the description?

answers: It moves from his general appearance to his bodily features and finally to his sweetness and relationship
It moves from the watchmen to the city and finally to the garden
It moves from his disappearance to the search and finally to the woman’s wounds
medium.explanation: The passage begins with his overall appearance, describes his features, and ends with his sweetness and personal importance.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the structure of the passage?

answers: Outstanding and distinguished among many
Hidden from everyone
Weak and tired
medium.explanation: The phrase presents the beloved as surpassing and standing out among countless others.

answers: The description expresses how her love makes him appear perfect, sweet, and personally near
The description proves that she does not know him
The description shows that she cares only about his clothing
challenge.explanation: The beautiful imagery reflects both his appearance and the depth of her affection for him.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the beloved’s outward description and the woman’s feelings?

answers: The mention of the watchmen
The many images of gold, jewels, ivory, marble, Lebanon, and cedars
The fact that he withdraws and is gone
challenge.explanation: The elevated images create an idealized portrait that goes beyond ordinary physical identification.
challenge.q: Which detail most strongly shows that the beloved is presented as an ideal of beauty rather than merely identified?

answers: It presents him only as a beautiful figure
It joins his beauty with a personal and intimate relationship
It identifies him as one of the watchmen
challenge.explanation: The closing statement connects the beloved’s splendor with closeness, affection, and friendship.
challenge.q: How does “This is my beloved, and this is my friend” deepen the description?
